passage:
A new bench was placed under the old tree in the park. At first, people did not notice it. They walked past it as usual.
Then an old man began sitting there every afternoon. He brought bread for birds and a small radio. A young mother often stopped near the bench while her baby slept. Two students sat there to study after school.
Within a month, the bench became a small meeting place. People who had seen each other for years finally began to talk.
The tree had always given shade, but the bench gave people a reason to stay. Sometimes a place changes not because it becomes larger or newer, but because it gives people time to stop.
